concepts.heading: The Spectrum from Enthusiastic to Coercive
concepts.plain: A yes can be eager, unsure or forced. Only the eager kind really counts.

concepts.heading: What Enthusiastic Consent Looks Like
concepts.alt: Two guides leaning toward each other with bright smiles, one giving two thumbs up, sparkles between them
concepts.plain: A real yes shows in the whole person: words, body and mood.

concepts.heading: What Coercion Looks Like
concepts.alt: A guide leaning back with an uneasy face as a large cartoon hand pushes on his shoulder
concepts.plain: Coercion means pushing, guilting or wearing someone down until they give in.

concepts.heading: Recognizing the Gray Areas
concepts.alt: A guide weighing a green tick against a red cross on a balance scale, looking unsure, a grey fog cloud behind her
concepts.plain: Sometimes you went along with something you did not want. That matters too.

concepts.heading: Coercion Is Never the Receiver's Fault
concepts.alt: She rests a supportive hand on his shoulder, a small shield with a heart floating beside them
concepts.plain: If you were pressured, it is not your fault. It is on the person who pushed.

concepts.heading: Building a Practice of Enthusiastic Consent

checks.prompt: Riley says no twice. Their date keeps asking and sulking until Riley gives in. What is this?
checks.explanation: Coercion. Coercion involves using pressure, manipulation, or power to override someone's ability to freely choose.

checks.after: Coercion Is Never the Receiver's Fault
checks.prompt: Someone was pressured into saying yes. Where does the responsibility lie?
options: With the person who applied the pressure
With the person who gave in
checks.explanation: With the person who applied the pressure. Regardless of the circumstances, if someone was coerced, the responsibility lies with the person who applied pressure — not the person who experienced it.

73b2086f-2265-4dec-8bb1-da6079185930.takeaway: Only a free, eager yes counts. A yes won by pressure is not consent.

concepts.heading: Navigating Consent Across Multiple Relationships
concepts.alt: Three guides sitting in a circle talking, each holding up a green tick card
concepts.plain: The same consent basics apply. There are just more people to check in with.

concepts.heading: Ongoing Renegotiation
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting at a table with a calendar and two coffee cups, going over a checklist together
concepts.plain: Agreements need a fresh look often, because things keep changing.

concepts.heading: Consent to One Thing Is Not Consent to Everything
concepts.alt: A guide holding up one puzzle piece marked with a green tick while other puzzle pieces float untouched
concepts.plain: A yes to one thing, or one person, is not a yes to everything.

concepts.heading: Metamour Agreements and Consent Networks
concepts.alt: Linked together by a string of hearts like a network, waving at each other
concepts.plain: Your choices reach your partner's other partners too, so keep them in mind.

concepts.heading: Practical Tools for Multi-Partner Consent
concepts.plain: Simple habits help: regular check-ins and clear, shared agreements.

concepts.heading: When Consent Gets Complicated
concepts.alt: A guide holding a glowing brain in one hand and a worried heart in the other, comparing them
concepts.plain: Your head can say yes while your heart says "not yet". Say so out loud.

checks.after: Consent to One Thing Is Not Consent to Everything
checks.prompt: Kai agreed that their partner could go on dates. The partner assumes overnight stays are fine too. Which idea was missed?
options: Consent to one thing is not consent to everything
checks.explanation: Consent to one thing is not consent to everything. For example: Consenting to your partner dating someone new does not mean consenting to specific sexual activities with that person.

checks.prompt: Jo said yes and truly meant it, but now feels knots in their stomach about it. What does the lesson say about this?
options: A yes in your head can still be hard in your heart
checks.explanation: A yes in your head can still be hard in your heart. Sometimes in ENM, a partner may consent to something intellectually but struggle with it emotionally.

950ac1ad-1eea-473c-bc94-0466f2b4db98.takeaway: With more partners, check in more often. A yes to one thing or one person is never a yes to all.

concepts.heading: When Consent Is Violated: Recognition, Response, and Healing
concepts.plain: Consent gets broken in every kind of community. Knowing what to do helps.

concepts.heading: Recognizing When Consent Was Absent
concepts.alt: A guide looking thoughtfully at a traffic light showing red, one hand on her chest
concepts.plain: Sometimes it is obvious. Sometimes you only see it later.

concepts.heading: Responding When Someone Tells You Their Consent Was Violated
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting close, she listens with full attention while he speaks, a heart-shaped ear icon above her
concepts.plain: If someone tells you, listen first. Believe them. Do not argue.

concepts.heading: Community Accountability vs. Punishment
concepts.alt: Three guides standing in a circle around a small growing plant, hands open, repairing together
concepts.plain: The goal is to repair harm and change behaviour, not only to punish.

concepts.heading: Finding Support
concepts.alt: A guide holding a phone in one hand and a life ring in the other, offering help
concepts.plain: If this happened to you, you deserve help. You do not have to carry it alone.

concepts.heading: Your Role in Consent Culture
concepts.alt: Four guides standing side by side with linked arms, a big shield with a heart in front of them
concepts.plain: Everyone helps build a place where "no" is respected.

checks.after: Responding When Someone Tells You Their Consent Was Violated
checks.prompt: A friend tells you their consent was violated. What is the most helpful first response?
options: Ask what they did to cause it
checks.explanation: Listen without doubting them. Do not question their experience or perception.

checks.prompt: A community wants someone to understand the harm they caused and change, not just be thrown out. What is this approach called?
checks.explanation: Accountability. Many communities, especially in ENM and kink spaces, are moving toward accountability-based models rather than purely punitive ones.

d8cb5e39-e96d-4392-8cf7-3cbe2eb3d051.takeaway: When consent is broken: believe, support, and aim to repair the harm.

hero.alt: A guide holding up a carton of five fries, one for each letter of FRIES

mnemonic.caption: Five letters to remember what a real yes looks like.

concepts.heading: Understanding Consent Through the FRIES Model
concepts.alt: Two guides learning together
concepts.plain: Consent is more than hearing a yes. FRIES is five things to check.

concepts.heading: Freely Given
concepts.alt: One person offers an open hand while the other takes her time to decide, an open padlock between them
concepts.plain: A real yes comes with no pressure, guilt or fear.

concepts.heading: Reversible
concepts.alt: A guide holding an undo arrow sign and raising a hand to pause
concepts.plain: Anyone can change their mind at any time, even in the middle.

concepts.heading: Informed
concepts.alt: Two guides reading a checklist together under a lightbulb
concepts.plain: You can only say yes to what you actually know about.

concepts.heading: Enthusiastic
concepts.alt: A guide jumping for joy beside a speech bubble with a heart
concepts.plain: Look for a happy, eager yes. Silence or "I guess" is not a yes.

concepts.heading: Specific
concepts.alt: A guide pointing at a list where only one box is ticked
concepts.plain: A yes to one thing is not a yes to anything else.

concepts.heading: Why This Matters
concepts.alt: Two guides sharing a high five

checks.prompt: Sam said yes to staying over. Later that night Sam says, “I’ve changed my mind. I’m going to head home.” Which part of FRIES covers this?
checks.explanation: Reversible. Anyone can change their mind at any time, for any reason, even if they said yes before.

checks.prompt: Jo asks, “Want to kiss?” Riley shrugs and says, “I guess so…” Which part of FRIES is missing?
checks.explanation: Enthusiastic. Look for a genuine, excited yes. Silence, hesitation, or “I guess so” are not enthusiasm.

20612de7-667f-4c06-aa0c-9955d9964a70.takeaway: A real yes is freely given, can be taken back, informed, eager and specific.
